# Agent platform — Key Files

> Per-file reference table for `admin/src`, `runtime/`, `lib/` and `scripts/bin`. See [agent.md](./agent.md) for the architecture, HTTP surfaces and data model, [admin-service.md](./admin-service.md) and [agent-runtime.md](./agent-runtime.md) for the module maps, and [agent-web-ui.md](./agent-web-ui.md) for the browser-facing surfaces. Coding-specialty files (the coding admin and agent extensions and the Shipwright plugin) are documented in the [shipwright repo](https://github.com/app-vitals/shipwright/blob/main/docs/agent-key-files.md).

## Admin service (`admin/src`)

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `admin/src/main.ts` | Standalone admin service entrypoint (Dockerfile `ENTRYPOINT`) and the composition root: the only file that picks the `AdminExtension`s. Exports `adminExtensions` (empty on the plain platform; downstream images replace this file) and calls `startAdmin(adminExtensions)` only under `import.meta.main`, so it stays import-safe. |
| `admin/src/admin-boot.ts` | `startAdmin(extensions = [])` — the admin platform boot sequence: Sentry → `prisma migrate deploy` → Prisma client → platform services → resolve extensions → routes (health, runtime API, admin CRUD API, accounts API, extension API routes, admin UI, extension UI routes) → the four platform sweepers (per-agent and account trial warning/expiry) → extension background passes → `Bun.serve` → graceful shutdown → fire-and-forget startup policy reconcile. Mounts `GET /health` (liveness, DB-independent) and `GET /health/ready` (readiness, DB-aware via `checkDbReady()`; returns 503 once a shutdown signal is received via `registerGracefulShutdown()` in `lib/graceful-shutdown.ts`). Imports no coding module. Order pinned by `admin-boot.boot-order.unit.test.ts`; excluded from the coverage gate as process wiring. |
| `admin/src/admin-boot-config.ts` | Env-driven boot helpers used by `startAdmin()`: `runMigrations()`, `buildProvisioner()` (K8s vs Noop, voice/policy/federation/chat-service wiring), `parseAnthropicFederation()` / `isAnthropicFederationEnabled()`, `buildDeletionClients()` (chat-service client for `deleteAgentFully()`, independent of K8s provisioning), `checkDbReady()`, `resolvePublicRepo()`, `resolveSessionAlertIntervalMs()`, `resolveTrialExpiryWarningDays()` and the boot constants. Unit-tested via `main.unit.test.ts`. |
| `admin/src/admin-extension.ts` | The `AdminExtension` seam between the admin platform and specialty-specific admin behavior (mirrors `runtime/agent-extension.ts`). All hooks optional: `services(ctx)`, `apiRoutes(ctx)`, `adminUiRoutes(ctx)`, `agentDetailCards(ctx)` (extra cards on `GET /admin/agents/:id`; a throwing card is omitted), `backgroundPasses(ctx)` (interval loops started after the platform sweepers), `serviceIntegrations(env)` and a static `openApi()` contribution folded into the generated spec. `resolveAdminExtensions()` calls the context hooks hook-by-hook in `ADMIN_EXTENSION_HOOK_ORDER`; no extension, or a hookless one, resolves to empty contributions, so the admin is the bare platform. |
| `admin/src/admin-spec.ts` | `buildPlatformAdminSpec()` builds the platform-only admin OpenAPI document (admin CRUD app + runtime app, no extension routes). It is the source of `admin/openapi.platform.json`; `admin/openapi.json` is the composed spec including extension contributions, and `lib/admin-types.ts` is the generated typed-client schema (`openapi-typescript`) the runtime's `HttpShipwrightRuntimeClient` uses. |
| `admin/src/api.ts` | Runtime API factory `createAgentRuntimeApp()` (OpenAPIHono app with OAS route definitions; DI for services) — the agent-facing `GET /agents/:id/config` and `GET /agents/:id/crons`. |
| `admin/src/agents-api.ts` | Admin CRUD factory `createAdminApp()` for the `/agents/*` admin API (the accounts API is mounted separately by `accounts-api.ts`). |
| `admin/src/api-auth.ts` | Combined admin auth middleware (`createAdminAuthMiddleware()`) and env-key parser (`parseAdminApiKeys()`) — bearer check order: env API keys (scope enforcement), then DB token via `agentTokenService`; the bearer path does not fall through to the session cookie on failure. Also hosts `requireScope()` and the platform read/ops scope constants. |
| `admin/src/caller-scope.ts` | `CallerScope` resolver (`all` or `scoped` to an account's and member's agents) shared by the admin UI, the session-visibility helpers and the auth middleware; account membership counts only when the self-serve flag is on. |
| `admin/src/agent-ask.ts` | Agent-to-agent ask: `POST /agents/{id}/ask` and `GET /agents/{id}/asks`, the `AgentAskService` audit store and the gate order (flag, caller, chat client, depth, allowlist, target). Never stores the question text. |
| `admin/src/agent-ask-config.ts` | `parseAgentAskConfig(env)` reads `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ENABLED` (literal `enabled`) and the `from>to` `SHIPWRIGHT_AGENT_ASK_ALLOWLIST`; a malformed pair throws. `isAskAllowed()` is the directional pair check. |
| `admin/src/chat-credential-config.ts` | `parseChatCredentialConfig(env)` reads `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_TOKEN_MINT_ENABLED` (literal `enabled`) for the chat-credential mint/revoke routes in `agents-api.ts`. |
| `admin/src/platform-doc-route.ts` | `mountPlatformDoc()` mounts `GET /doc` (the platform OpenAPI document) behind the admin auth middleware only when `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_DOC_ENABLED` is `enabled`. |
| `admin/src/openapi-schemas.ts` | Zod schemas for the admin and runtime APIs — entity types (Agent, AgentCronJob, AgentTool, AgentToken, AgentPlugin, accounts), request bodies, runtime response shapes (`AgentConfigResponse`, `RuntimeError`), and the common `Error`/`Ok` shapes. `z` is imported from `@hono/zod-openapi` for `.openapi()` metadata. |
| `admin/src/agents.ts` | `AgentService` — agent CRUD (`create()`, `delete()`, `getDetail()`, `listAll()`, `listByIds()`, `listOptions()`, `searchByName()`, `updateFields()`, `updateAndRefresh()`, `runTransaction()`); write methods accept an optional Prisma transaction `client` so callers can compose atomic writes. Also exports the standalone `createAgent()` — parses the multiline form fields (repos, allowlists, member emails), creates the agent row, seeds `AgentTool`/`AgentPlugin` from the resolved type manifest, attaches repos/allowlists/members, stores Claude credentials, and reconciles system crons. All DB writes run in a single transaction with explicit rollback; Kubernetes provisioning (an external side effect) runs after the commit and cron reconciliation is best-effort. Returns a discriminated `CreateAgentResult` (`{ok: true, agent, ...}` or `{ok: false, errorCode}`) whose codes map directly into `/admin/agents/new?error=…`. Called by the `POST /admin/agents` handler in `admin-ui.ts`. |
| `admin/src/admin-ui.ts` | Admin UI factory `createAdminUIApp()` — server-rendered Hono app: login (Google / Okta OAuth, optional dev login), agent list/detail/new, per-agent mutation routes (envs, repos, settings, crons, tools, tokens, members, delete, sync-manifest), Slack and GitHub provisioning (`/admin/agents/:id/connect-slack`, `.../connect-github`, plus the legacy `GET /admin/provision` redirect to `/admin/agents/new`), chat threads and messages (including multipart attachment upload and the attachment proxy), PWA routes (manifest, service worker, offline page, icons) and Web Push subscribe/unsubscribe/notify. `POST /admin/agents` is admin-only and delegates to `createAgent()`; Slack/GitHub provisioning on creation is gated server-side to in-cluster runtimes, and when both are requested the GitHub PAT is stored first and Slack's OAuth redirect returned last. Dependencies come in through `AdminUIDeps` (`chatClient`, `devAuthEnabled`, `pushService`, `vapidPublicKey`, `pwaAssetsDir`, …); without `chatClient` the chat routes render in degraded mode. See [agent-web-ui.md](./agent-web-ui.md). |
| `admin/src/dev-auth-guard.ts` | `isDevAuthAllowed(env)` — pure predicate over an injected env object. Returns `true` only when `ADMIN_DEV_AUTH=true` and `NODE_ENV !== "production"`. |
| `admin/src/admin-ui-pages.ts` | Page rendering functions: `renderLoginPage`, `renderAgentsPage`, `renderNewLocalAgentPage`, `renderAgentDetailPage`, the GitHub/Slack provisioning step pages (`renderGithubAppManifestRedirectPage`, `renderGithubAppInstallPage`, `renderGithubAppInstalledPage`, `renderProvisionXappTokenPage`, `renderProvisionCompletePage`), `renderChatPage`, `renderChatThreadPage` and the shared `renderChatMessageBubble()`, plus helpers (`renderMarkdown`, `relativeTime`, `cronOutcomeStyle`, `ERROR_KIND_LABELS`). The agent detail page is a set of collapsible accordion sections, includes cron-run history per cron, and renders the GitHub Installations card; the new-agent page hides the Slack/GitHub sections client-side for the self-hosted runtime (server-side gating lives in `admin-ui.ts`). The chat thread page shows message bubbles with error-kind badges and Retry for recoverable kinds, per-message and thread-level token/cost stats, inline audio attachments (decided once in the shared bubble renderer so live polls and reloads match), and a mobile off-canvas thread drawer. |
| `admin/src/admin-ui-layout.ts` | `renderAdminPage()` — the shared page shell (head, toolbar, nav, content slot) used by every admin page. |
| `admin/src/http-chat-client.ts` | Typed HTTP client for admin-side chat-service access. Exports the `ChatClient` interface (for DI), `HttpChatClient` (injectable `fetchFn`), `NoopChatClient` (no-op fallback) and the `ChatThread`, `ChatMessage` (optional `errorKind`, attachment fields, `tokens: MessageTokens`, `costUsd`), `ThreadStats`, `ListThreadsResult` and option types. `getThreadStats(threadId)` returns aggregated token/cost stats; `createMessage()` accepts an optional attachment (`filename`, `size`, `bytes`). Used by the `/admin/chat*` routes; smoke tests mock at the `ChatClient` interface level. |
| `admin/src/admin-ui-styles.ts` | Shared CSS helpers and responsive breakpoint constants: `baseStyles()`, `renderAdminToolbar()`, `BREAKPOINT_MOBILE_MAX` (640 px) and `BREAKPOINT_TABLET_MAX` (960 px). Tests assert against the constants rather than hardcoded pixel strings. Re-exports `escapeHtml` for safe string interpolation. |
| `admin/src/google-auth-client.ts` | `GoogleAuthClient` interface + `HttpGoogleAuthClient` — typed Google OAuth2 token exchange and user profile lookup; injected into the admin UI for testability. |
| `admin/src/okta-auth-client.ts` | `OktaAuthClient` interface + `HttpOktaAuthClient` — typed Okta OIDC authorization URL generation, token exchange and user profile lookup. Mirrors the three-method shape of `GoogleAuthClient` (`getAuthorizationUrl`, `exchangeCode`, `getUserInfo`). |
| `admin/src/slack-provisioning-client.ts` | `SlackProvisioningClient` interface + `HttpSlackProvisioningClient` — drives Slack app management: `createAppManifest()` returns `appId`, `oauthRedirectUrl`, `clientId`, `clientSecret` and `signingSecret` from `apps.manifest.create`; `deleteApp(xoxpToken, appId)` calls `apps.manifest.delete`; `exchangeOAuthCode()` exchanges the OAuth callback code for a bot token via `oauth.v2.access`. Also exports `buildAgentManifest(appName, redirectUri?)` (per-agent app manifest with `agent_view` description/suggested prompts and event subscriptions) and `AGENT_BOT_SCOPES`, the canonical bot scope list shared by provisioning and the sync-manifest flow. |
| `admin/src/slack-provisioning-service.ts` | `SlackProvisioningService` — Slack app-manifest-creation/OAuth orchestration shared by the per-agent connect-slack routes, inline Slack connection at agent creation, and the legacy provisioning entry. Exports `PROVISION_STATE_COOKIE` / `PROVISION_STATE_TTL_SECONDS`; methods: `createAppManifest(agentName, xoxpToken, redirectUri)`, `signProvisionState(agentId, creds, extra?)` (JWT for the provision-state cookie), `startConnect(agentId, xoxpToken, redirectUri)` (validates the agent, creates the manifest, returns a signed token + OAuth URL), `completeConnect(rawStateCookie, code, fallbackRedirectUri)` (verifies state, exchanges the code for `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN`; outcomes `invalid_state`, `missing_code`, `exchange_failed`, `reinstalled`, `needs_app_token`) and `saveAppToken(agentId, xappToken)` (stores `SLACK_APP_TOKEN` and reconciles system crons). No HTTP mechanics — cookies, redirects and HTML stay in the routes. |
| `admin/src/github-provisioning-service.ts` | `GithubProvisioningService` — GitHub App manifest-flow and PAT provisioning orchestration, shared by the per-agent connect-github routes (`POST /admin/agents/:id/connect-github`, `GET .../callback`, `GET .../installed`), inline GitHub auth at agent creation, and the legacy provisioning entry. Exports `GITHUB_PROVISION_STATE_COOKIE`, `GITHUB_PROVISION_STATE_TTL_SECONDS` and `GITHUB_ORG_PATTERN`; methods: `startPatConnect(agentId, ghPat)` (stores `GH_TOKEN` directly), `startAppManualConnect(agentId, {ghAppId, ghAppInstallationId, ghAppPrivateKey})` (validates numeric IDs + PEM key, stores `GH_APP_ID` / `GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` / `GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`), `signProvisionState(agentId, githubOrg)` (HS256 JWT for the cookie) and `startAppAutoConnect(agentId, githubOrg, {redirectUri, setupUrl})` (validates the org against `GITHUB_ORG_PATTERN`, builds the manifest via `buildAgentAppManifest`, returns the signed state for the manifest redirect), plus the callback/install completion steps. See [github-multi-org.md](./github-multi-org.md). |
| `admin/src/github-app-provisioning-client.ts` | `GithubAppProvisioningClient` interface + `HttpGithubAppProvisioningClient` — GitHub "create a GitHub App from a manifest" flow: the browser is redirected to GitHub's manifest endpoint, GitHub redirects back with a one-time `code`, and `exchangeManifestCode(code)` (POST `app-manifests/{code}/conversions`, unauthenticated per GitHub's spec) returns the app credentials (`appId`, `slug`, `pem`, `clientId`, `clientSecret`; the webhook secret is intentionally discarded since there is no webhook receiver). Also exports `buildAgentAppManifest(appName, opts?)` with configurable redirect/setup URIs and scoped permissions (contents:write, pull_requests:write, actions:read, workflows:write). The HTTP implementation takes optional `apiBase` and `fetchFn` overrides. |
| `admin/src/service-integration.ts` | `ServiceIntegration` interface (name, mint/revoke/list token client, token/URL env names, Secret key, url) for optional per-agent service integrations supplied by the composition root via `AdminExtension.serviceIntegrations(env)`. Extension integrations are processed in list order and always before the built-in chat-service integration (mint order, Secret keys, Deployment env, rollback, and `${name}-tokens` deletion steps). `provisionableIntegrations()` filters to those with a `url`. The platform provisioner, manifest and deletion code name no specific service. |
| `admin/src/coding-task-store-provisioning-client.ts` | `TaskStoreProvisioningClient` interface + `HttpTaskStoreProvisioningClient` + `NoopTaskStoreProvisioningClient` — mints/revokes/lists per-agent task-store API tokens (`POST /tokens`, `DELETE /tokens/:id`, `GET /tokens` with admin auth; the list is filtered client-side by agent). Nothing in the plain platform imports it: a downstream composition root wraps it in a `ServiceIntegration` so the provisioner stores the token in the agent Secret and injects it into the Deployment, and deletion revokes it. |
| `admin/src/chat-service-provisioning-client.ts` | `ChatServiceProvisioningClient` interface + `HttpChatServiceProvisioningClient` + `NoopChatServiceProvisioningClient` — mints/revokes per-agent chat-service API tokens (`POST /tokens`, `DELETE /tokens/:id` with admin auth; the noop returns empty strings). Integrated into `KubernetesAgentProvisioner`: when `config.chatService` is set, `provision()` mints a token (labeled `agent:<agentId>`), stores it in the agent Secret (key `chat-service-token`) and injects it into the Deployment; rollback revokes it. Also exports `listTokensForAgent(agentId)` (filtered client-side) and `deleteThreadsForAgent(agentId)` (paginates `GET /threads?agentId=` and deletes each thread, tolerating 404s) — both wired into `deleteAgentFully()`. |
| `admin/src/attachment-validation.ts` | Pure attachment validation and audio filename detection. `validateAttachment()` checks size (max 10 MB, `MAX_ATTACHMENT_BYTES`), MIME type (allowlist: images, PDFs, JSON, text, SVG, and `audio/webm`, `audio/webm;codecs=opus`, `audio/ogg` for mic-recorded blobs) and filename, returning a discriminated result (413 too-large, 415 unsupported-type on failure). Used by the message upload endpoint before files reach the chat service. `audioContentTypeForFilename()` maps an audio extension to a real `audio/*` Content-Type for the attachment-proxy route (`.webm` → `audio/webm`, `.mp3` → `audio/mpeg`; `null` for non-audio) and `isAudioFilename()` is the boolean wrapper for audio-vs-badge branching in templates. |
| `admin/src/agent-provisioner.ts` | `AgentProvisioner` interface + `KubernetesAgentProvisioner` (real K8s provisioning via `HttpKubernetesClient`) + `NoopAgentProvisioner` (DB-only). The K8s provisioner creates a per-agent PVC (persistent home), Secret (credentials) and Deployment (agent container), building specs with `agent-manifest.ts`. `provision()`: PVC → Secret with the agent token plus a token per service integration and the optional chat-service token → Deployment; on failure it rolls back the Secret (best-effort) and revokes the tokens it minted. With `perAgentIdentity` configured (per-agent Anthropic identity mode, wired in `buildProvisioner`), `provision()` first requires an owner email (else an `UnprocessableEntityError` before anything is created), then creates a Kubernetes ServiceAccount named like the Deployment, an Anthropic service account (added to the workspace) and a federation rule (subject `system:serviceaccount:<namespace>:<sa>`, `workspace:inference`, 600 s) through `AnthropicIdentityClient`, saving each ID via `AgentAnthropicIdentityService` immediately after its create; saved IDs are reused on retry, a create conflict is recovered by find-by-name, and a later failure archives/deletes only what that call created. `deprovision()` deletes the Deployment, Secret and PVC. `reconcile(targets, { policyOnly })` rolls agents whose Claude policy or federation wiring drifted. |
| `admin/src/startup-policy-reconcile.ts` | `runStartupPolicyReconcile({ agentService, provisioner, logger })` — a one-shot policy-only reconcile fired once after `Bun.serve` (fire-and-forget, never delays serving). The chart passes the Claude policy hash to admin as an env var, so a policy change restarts admin; on boot this pass calls `provisioner.reconcile(targets, { policyOnly: true })`, rolling only agents whose policy or Anthropic federation wiring drifted. It runs whether or not a policy is configured (so agents lose the mount when the policy is disabled) and does nothing when `provisioner.canProvision` is false. Errors are logged, never thrown. Also exports `managedReconcileTargets(agents)` (drops self-hosted agents, maps `name` to `slug`), which `POST /agents/reconcile` shares. |
| `admin/src/agent-deletion.ts` | `deleteAgentFully(agentId, deps, opts)` — the shared teardown orchestration behind `DELETE /agents/:id` and the admin UI "danger zone". Idempotent steps: (1) read the Agent + AgentEnv rows; (2) K8s deprovision (Deployment, Secret, PVC), then remove the per-agent Anthropic identity when the agent has a saved one; (3) revoke each service integration's tokens; (4) revoke chat-service tokens and delete chat threads; (5) optionally delete the Slack app (gated on a supplied user token); (6) build the manual-cleanup checklist (`agent-deletion-checklist.ts`, which also lists any identity pieces still live after a failed step); (7) delete the Agent row LAST, only if every automatable step succeeded. A partial failure leaves the row so the caller can retry; `NotFoundError` if the row is absent at call start. Returns `DeleteAgentResult` (`agentDeleted`, `completed`, `failed`, `manualStepsRequired`). |
| `admin/src/agent-manifest.ts` | Pure Kubernetes manifest builders: `buildAgentDeploymentManifest()`, `buildAgentPvcManifest()`, `buildAgentSecretManifest()`. Injects env for agent identity, voice (when enabled), each service integration (token from the Secret, URL as a plain value) and the chat service (`SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_TOKEN` / `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL`). `resolveAgentContainerResources(overrides?)` merges per-field overrides (CPU request, memory request/limit, ephemeral storage) onto the defaults (500m cpu / 2Gi memory request / 8Gi memory limit / 4Gi ephemeral storage, no CPU limit). When `AgentDeploymentOpts.claudePolicy` (`{ configMapName, hash? }`) is set the Deployment gains a read-only ConfigMap volume (`claude-policy`) plus a hash annotation so a policy change rolls the pod; `AgentDeploymentOpts` also carries the Anthropic federation wiring (projected token volume, `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_ENV_NAMES`). Constants: `AGENT_HEALTH_PORT`, `AGENT_HOME_MOUNT_PATH`, `TENANT_LABEL`; `sanitizeAgentName()` derives resource names. |
| `admin/src/agent-envs.ts` | `AgentEnvService` — encrypted key/value store per agent and config-bundle assembly (`getConfigBundle`). Rejects Anthropic credential keys for non-self-hosted agents when federation is enabled (see `anthropic-credential-guard.ts`). |
| `admin/src/anthropic-credential-guard.ts` | Shared guard for Anthropic workload identity federation. Exports `ANTHROPIC_CREDENTIAL_KEYS` (`CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY`, `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN`), `isAnthropicCredentialKey()`, `anthropicCredentialKeysIn()` and `AnthropicCredentialsBlockedError` (HTTP 400, code `anthropic_credentials_blocked_federation`). Used by `AgentEnvService`. |
| `admin/src/anthropic-identity-client.ts` | `AnthropicIdentityClient` interface + `HttpAnthropicIdentityClient` — manages an agent's Anthropic identity through the Admin API using `@anthropic-ai/sdk` typed resources with an injected `fetch`: `createServiceAccount`, `addServiceAccountToWorkspace`, `createFederationRule`, `archiveFederationRule`, `archiveServiceAccount`, and the paged find-by-name fallbacks `findServiceAccountByName` / `findFederationRuleByName` (the list endpoints have no name filter, so every `next_page` is followed). Every response is zod-parsed; 409 surfaces as `AnthropicConflictError`, a persistent 401 as `AnthropicAuthError` (after one token re-exchange); errors carry only status / error type / request-id, never tokens. |
| `admin/src/anthropic-federated-token-provider.ts` | `FederatedTokenProvider` — signs the admin pod in to Anthropic by workload identity federation: re-reads the projected ServiceAccount token file on every exchange (kubelet rotation), exchanges it via `POST /v1/oauth/token` (jwt-bearer grant), and caches the access token until shortly before `expires_in` using an injected `Clock`. The endpoint is not in the Anthropic OpenAPI spec, so it is exercised through a fake token exchange only. |
| `admin/src/fixtures/anthropic-openapi/` | Vendored Anthropic OpenAPI 3.1 spec (`mock-spec.json.gz`, from `anthropics/anthropic-sdk-typescript` at tag `sdk-v<SDK_VERSION>`) plus the `SDK_VERSION` marker, which must equal the exact `@anthropic-ai/sdk` version in `admin/package.json`. Kept gzipped. `anthropic-identity-fixture-spec.integration.test.ts` validates every recorded request/response against it. |
| `admin/src/agent-cron-jobs.ts` | `AgentCronJobService` — cron CRUD, `setEnabled()`, `list()` and `listWithRunSummary()` (crons enriched with last run time/outcome and today's run count), cron expression validation (`isValidCron`), and system-cron reconciliation. |
| `admin/src/agent-cron-runs.ts` | `AgentCronRunService` — `create()` (POST a run), `patch()` (record completion/progress), `list()` (paginated runs for one cron, with model breakdown), `listForAgent()` (paginated runs across an agent's crons with the cron relation included to avoid N+1; filters by cronId and outcome/skipped) and `listAcrossAgents()` (paginated runs across a set of agentIds, newest first; empty result for an empty list). `PatchAgentCronRunInput` carries run telemetry (`contextBaseline`, `contextFingerprint`, `pluginVersion`, `claudeCodeVersion`, `turns`, `toolCalls`) plus `modelBreakdown` and `skillUsage` arrays that upsert per-item by unique key. |
| `admin/src/agent-cron-run-stats.ts` | `AgentCronRunStatsService` — aggregates `AgentCronRun` token columns (via `$queryRaw`, since Prisma `groupBy` can't do the `AgentCronJob` LEFT JOIN) into `totals`, `byAgent`, `byCron`, `byModel`, `daily`, `byCronModel` and `byPhase`, plus `bySkill`, `baselines` (first-turn context baseline per fingerprint/model/phase) and the per-phase outcome series (`CronRunOutcomes`). Skipped runs are excluded from token aggregations. See [agent-api-ops.md](./agent-api-ops.md#cron-run-stats). |
| `admin/src/agent-tools.ts` | `AgentToolService` — manages allowed tool patterns per agent. |
| `admin/src/agent-tokens.ts` | `AgentTokenService` — manages scoped API tokens per agent (raw token returned once at creation; only the SHA-256 hash persisted). |
| `admin/src/agent-plugins.ts` | `AgentPluginService` — manages installed Claude Code plugins per agent: `add(agentId, name, version?)` (upsert), `list(agentId)` (ordered by createdAt), `remove(agentId, pluginId)` and `removeByName(agentId, name)`; throws `NotFoundError` when the plugin doesn't exist or belongs to a different agent. |
| `admin/src/pwa.ts` | PWA shell builders backing the [PWA shell section](./agent-web-ui.md) of agent-web-ui.md. Exports `PWA_ASSETS_DIR` (`admin/pwa-assets/`), `PWA_ICONS` (allowlist served by `GET /admin/icons/:filename`), `buildManifest(startUrl?)` (served at `GET /admin/manifest.webmanifest`; default start URL `/admin/chat`), `sanitizeStartUrl(path)` (same-origin `/admin/...` allowlist gate: rejects external URLs, traversal, protocol-relative/`javascript:` values and non-navigable asset/auth routes; malformed percent-encoding is a rejection), `getPrecacheList()`, `shouldCachePwaRequest(path, method)`, `buildServiceWorkerBody()` (the full `/admin/sw.js` source with `install`/`activate`/`fetch`/`push`/`notificationclick` handlers), `buildOfflinePageHtml()` and `renderPwaHeadTags(appBaseUrl)` (manifest link with a per-page `?start=` rewrite plus iOS meta tags). Pure; icons are the committed PNGs in `admin/pwa-assets/icons/`. |
| `admin/src/push-content.ts` | Notification-content policy as pure functions — deliberately austere, since a notification renders on a locked phone. Exports `PushDetailLevel` (`"generic" \| "title" \| "preview"`), `DEFAULT_MAX_DETAIL` (`"title"`, the operator ceiling default), `resolveDetailLevel(ceiling, optIn)` (effective level = min of operator ceiling and user opt-in), `buildNotificationPayload()` (assembles `{title, body, url}` per level; free text is scrubbed of id/repo/path/cost-shaped substrings, over-redacting rather than leaking; agent name, ids, repo names, paths and costs never appear at any level — only the deep-link `url` carries a threadId) and the sibling session-notification policy (`SessionNotificationKind`, `NotificationSession`, `buildSessionNotificationPayload(level, kind, session)`). |
| `admin/src/push-crypto.ts` | Hand-rolled RFC 8291 (Web Push message encryption, `aes128gcm`) and RFC 8292 (VAPID) primitives on Bun's `node:crypto` rather than the `web-push` package (small dependency tree; correctness pinned to the RFC 8291 Appendix A test vector in `push-crypto.unit.test.ts`). Exports `base64UrlEncode()` / `base64UrlDecode()` and `encryptPushPayload(args)` (ECDH P-256 + HKDF-SHA256 + AES-128-GCM). Pure — no Hono, Prisma or network; the send lives in `push-sender.ts`. |
| `admin/src/push-sender.ts` | `PushSender` — sends an encrypted Web Push message to one or many subscriptions, constructed with an injected `fetchImpl` (no global `fetch` override). Signs the VAPID JWT (ES256) via `node:crypto` and encrypts the payload via `push-crypto.ts`. Delivery contract: 2xx → delivered; `404`/`410` → subscription gone, pruned; any other failure (or network throw) → not pruned (transient); one failure never blocks the rest. Exports `VapidConfig`, `PushSubscriptionLike` and `isPushEnabled(config)` (`true` only when public key, private key and subject are ALL set). |
| `admin/src/push-service.ts` | `PushService` — orchestrates the "your agent replied" notification and owns all write access to the `ChatThreadWatch` / `PushSubscription` models (route handlers never touch those Prisma delegates directly). Targeting flows through `ChatThreadWatch`: only users who sent a message in a thread are notified when the agent replies. Each subscription's payload is built at `min(operator ceiling, that subscription's opt-in)` via `push-content.ts`; subscriptions the provider reports gone are pruned via `push-sender.ts`. Constructed with an injected `fetchImpl`; `admin-boot.ts` only constructs it when `isPushEnabled()` is true. Exports `PushPrismaLike` (the narrow Prisma slice it touches) and `NotificationSession`. |
| `admin/src/admin-ui-push-test.ts` | `registerPushTestRoute(app, deps)` — `POST /admin/push/test`, the "Send test notification" route: admin-only (`403` otherwise), sends a fixed, detail-free payload (`PUSH_TEST_PAYLOAD`) to the *caller's own* subscriptions via `PushService.sendToUsers()` and returns `{ok, delivered, pruned}`; `delivered: 0` means the account has no live subscription. Scoped to `c.var.userEmail`, so a request body can't page another user; 503 when push is disabled. Also exports `renderPushTestControl()`. Not mounted by the plain platform — a downstream UI extension registers it. |
| `admin/src/push-toggle.ts` | `renderPushToggle(args)` — the push-notification toggle fragment spliced into the chat thread page. When push is disabled server-side (no VAPID public key threaded in) it returns `""` so the page degrades to the no-push layout. Its client script requests `Notification` permission only inside the click handler (never on load), never re-requests after `"denied"` (shows static guidance), and treats an undefined `PushManager` on non-standalone iOS Safari as "not installed" ("Add to Home Screen" guidance). Subscribes via `navigator.serviceWorker.ready` → `pushManager.subscribe`. Exports `PushToggleArgs` and `renderPushToggle()`. |
| `admin/src/trial-expiry-sweeper.ts` | `TrialExpirySweeper` — the per-agent *lockdown* half of trial expiry (the warning half is `trial-expiry-warning-sweeper.ts`; account-level expiry is `account-trial-expiry-sweeper.ts` / `account-trial-warning-sweeper.ts`). One of the admin service's background loops, registered via `setInterval` in `admin-boot.ts`; cadence from `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TRIAL_EXPIRY_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS` (default 60 s, `resolveTrialExpirySweepIntervalMs()` falls back on unset/blank/non-numeric/non-positive values). Each tick finds every enabled `AgentCronJob` of an agent whose `trialExpiresAt` has passed and disables it via `AgentCronJobService.setEnabled()`. It deliberately does **not** deprovision the agent — a trial ending should not destroy a workspace the customer may convert to paid; `isTrialExpired()` in `runtime/slack.ts` is the other half of the lockdown, blocking inbound Slack messages. `tick()` resolves to `{ disabled }` and never throws; per-row failures are caught individually. Naturally idempotent. |
| `admin/src/trial-expiry-warning-sweeper.ts` | `TrialExpiryWarningSweeper` — the per-agent *warning* half of trial expiry, a separate module from the lockdown sweeper (different cadence, counters and log prefix `[trial-expiry-warning-sweeper]`). Ticks hourly (`DEFAULT_TRIAL_EXPIRY_WARNING_SWEEP_INTERVAL_MS`); the window in days comes from `SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN_TRIAL_EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS` via `resolveTrialExpiryWarningDays()` (`undefined` on unset/blank/invalid, so the sweeper's `DEFAULT_TRIAL_EXPIRY_WARNING_DAYS` of 3 applies). Each tick finds `Agent` rows with `trialExpiresAt` set and `trialExpiryWarnedAt` null and, inside the firing band (up to `warningDays` before expiry and at most `graceDays` after), posts one Slack warning to that agent's **own** `SLACK_BOT_TOKEN` / `SLACK_ALERT_CHANNEL` (decrypted per agent via `AgentEnvService.getConfigBundle`; admin holds no shared bot token), then stamps `trialExpiryWarnedAt` via `AgentService.updateFields()` so nobody is warned twice. |

## Agent runtime (`runtime/`, root `index.ts`)

The runtime is the container image's workload: `runtime/entrypoint-main.ts` runs the startup sequence and spawns the root `index.ts`, which calls `startAgent()` from `runtime/boot.ts`. See [agent-runtime.md](./agent-runtime.md) for the narrative.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `index.ts` | Agent server entrypoint, spawned by `runtime/entrypoint.ts`. The composition root of the plain platform: it calls `startAgent([])` with no extensions; downstream images replace this file with one that passes their extension factories. |
| `runtime/boot.ts` | `startAgent(extensions)` — the runtime boot sequence. `extensions` are `AgentExtensionFactory` functions built once the runtime context exists and folded by `composeExtensions()`. Imports no coding module. Sequence: `ensureAgentHome` → health server (binds immediately so kubelet probes stay green) → console prefix monkeypatch via `buildLogPrefix()` and Sentry init (no-op without `SENTRY_DSN`) → `runMiseStartup` + plugin install → config sync (every 60 s: fetch the agent config bundle, apply env through the federation guard, refresh the synced refs, re-run GitHub App installation discovery via `reconcileGitHubInstallations()`, auto-clone newly-configured repos via `syncClonedRepos()`, and retry Slack Bolt startup and GitHub App auth via `startSlackIfPossible()` / `startGitHubAuthIfPossible()` so credentials that arrive after boot activate without a pod restart) → `reconcileSystemCrons` (best-effort) → cron sync loop (60 s) → chat poller (when `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_URL` and `SHIPWRIGHT_CHAT_SERVICE_TOKEN` are set) → Slack Bolt Socket Mode app → graceful SIGTERM/SIGINT shutdown. A separate periodic interval (`SHIPWRIGHT_PR_STATE_RECONCILER_INTERVAL_MS`, default 45 min) runs the runtime's own pass (`worktree-reaper`) followed by the extension's `periodicPasses`, each in its own try/catch. |
| `runtime/agent-extension.ts` | The `AgentExtension` seam between the generic runtime and specialty behavior. Hooks (all optional): `onConfigSync(bundle)`, `periodicPasses`, `onCronJobs(jobs)`, `classifyCronJobs(jobs)` (default `classifyAllGeneric`), `dispatchLoop(loopCronId)`. `planCronSchedule()` calls `onCronJobs` before `classifyCronJobs` on every cron-sync tick; `runPeriodicPasses()` runs passes in order, each in its own try/catch with a non-fatal `tick failed` log; `composeExtensions()` folds factories into one extension. Imports no coding module. |
| `runtime/entrypoint-main.ts` | Production CLI entry point (Dockerfile `ENTRYPOINT`) — wires real deps and calls `runEntrypoint()`. It does not start a health server: it runs the startup sequence and spawns the root `index.ts` as a subprocess, and `index.ts` owns the single health server on `SHIPWRIGHT_HEALTH_PORT` (default `3459`); a second listener here would fail with `EADDRINUSE`. |
| `runtime/entrypoint.ts` | Container startup sequence (`runEntrypoint()`), dependency-injected for testability: validates vars, fetches config, applies env, symlinks `~/.claude`, runs GitHub auth + mise (non-fatal — failures are logged without blocking startup) + plugin install, then spawns the server. |
| `runtime/anthropic-federation-guard.ts` | Defense-in-depth guard for Anthropic workload identity federation. When `ANTHROPIC_FEDERATION_RULE_ID` is in the pod env, `filterAnthropicCredentials()` drops `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` / `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` / `ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN` and deletes them from `process.env`; `applyEnvToProcess()` applies a config-bundle env through that filter (used by the entrypoint and `syncConfig()`). Logs key names only, once per key. |
| `runtime/cli-args.ts` | CLI argument parsing (`parseCliArgs()`) — `--agent-id`, `--api-url`, `--api-key` flags with env var fallbacks. Pure, no I/O. |
| `runtime/chat-poller.ts` | Chat poll loop: `createChatPoller(opts)` polls the chat service for pending messages, claims and runs them through Claude with per-thread session continuity (the injected `ChatRunner` owns a dedicated chat session store), and posts replies. Also exports `deriveReply` and the `TranscribeAudioFn` / `SynthesizeSpeechFn` types. `start()` skips a tick while the previous `pollOnce()` is still running. With `workspaceDir` set, a claimed message's attachment is fetched (`client.getAttachment()`) and written to `<workspaceDir>/uploads/{messageId}-{filename}`; audio attachments (`.webm`, `.ogg`, `.wav`, `.m4a`, `.mp3`) are transcribed when `transcribeAudioFn` is injected (falling back to a generic file-attached note on failure). `[speak:text]` markers in the reply are synthesized via `synthesizeSpeechFn` and attached (the marker is stripped regardless of synthesis success). **Heartbeat:** while the runner is in flight a plain timer (`heartbeatIntervalMs`, default 3 s) calls `client.heartbeat()`, deliberately not tied to Claude's per-turn progress since one long tool call can go quiet for minutes; the response carries `cancelRequested`, which triggers an `AbortController` passed to the runner. Aborted or failed runs post a reply with an `errorKind` (`cancelled`, `stalled`, `incomplete`) so the UI can render a badge and Retry. Heartbeat failures are logged and swallowed. |
| `runtime/http-chat-service-client.ts` | Typed HTTP client for the chat service REST API: `ChatServiceClient` (interface for DI), `HttpChatServiceClient` (injectable `fetchFn`), `ChatServiceClientError` (with `statusCode`) and the `Thread`, `Message`, `ListThreadsOptions`, `ListThreadsResult` types. `getAttachment(threadId, messageId)` returns the ephemeral attachment bytes (`null` when not found or already dropped) and `replyToMessage()` accepts optional attachment parameters (e.g. synthesized speech from `[speak:]`). Used by `createChatPoller()` to list threads, claim messages, send heartbeats, fetch attachments and post replies. |
| `runtime/piper-voice.ts` | Discovery-based Piper voice validation: `validatePiperVoice(requestedVoice?, readdirFn?)` scans the baked voices directory (`/app/agent/voices/`, hardcoded — not env-configurable; see `runtime/Dockerfile`), validates the requested voice against discovered `.onnx` / `.onnx.json` pairs and returns the resolved name. Returns `DEFAULT_PIPER_VOICE` when none is requested; an unknown voice logs a loud warning naming the requested and discovered voices and falls back to the default — it never throws. `resolvePiperVoicePaths(voiceName)` resolves a validated name to its model/config pair. Also exports `VOICES_DIR`. `readdirFn` is injectable so unit tests never touch the real filesystem. |
| `runtime/setup.ts` | Workspace bootstrapping: directory scaffolding, identity-file seeding (templates resolved per specialty via `resolveTemplatesDir()`, with per-file fallback to `runtime/workspace/`), layered `RUNTIME.md` (runtime-owned) and `SPECIALTY.md` (from the type's template dir, empty if none) rewritten on boot when changed, plugin installation (`installPlugins`, `findStalePluginSpecs`, baked-marketplace discovery) and `runMiseStartup`. Mise trust/install errors are non-fatal. Safe to call on every startup (idempotent). |
| `runtime/github-app-auth.ts` | `GitHubTokenManager` (`createGitHubTokenManager`) — installation-token cache with proactive 30-minute background refresh; `getBotIdentity()` / `fetchBotIdentity()` resolve the bot identity for git author config (testable with an injected `fetchFn`). |
| `runtime/setup-github-auth.ts` | `setupGitHubAuth()` — wires GitHub auth at agent startup and resolves `true` iff App auth activated. App path: engages only if a pin (`GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID`) is set OR installation discovery finds usable in-scope installations; mints tokens (injected `createTokenManager` or the installations manager), configures the git credential helper and author identity, and starts a background refresh. PAT path: runs `gh auth setup-git` when App auth does not engage. Not safely re-invokable after resolving `true` (each activation starts its own refresh interval), so callers gate repeat calls on the result (see `github-auth-startup.ts`). |
| `runtime/github-auth-deps.ts` | `buildGitHubAuthDeps(agentHome, scriptsBin, opts?)` — builds the production `GitHubAuthDeps` for `setupGitHubAuth()`, shared by `entrypoint-main.ts`'s one-shot boot call and the retry-on-tick call in `boot.ts` so both processes wire identical behavior. With `opts.withInstallations` (boot.ts only) it builds a `GitHubInstallationsManager` and returns installation-discovery deps (multi-installation support); without it (entrypoint) only the pinned-installation path is used. The single-installation path writes `gh-token` only; the installations path writes per-owner `gh-token.d/` files and never clobbers the entrypoint's `gh-token`. |
| `runtime/github-auth-startup.ts` | Mirrors `slack-startup.ts`'s ref/guard pattern for GitHub App auth. `startGitHubAuthIfPossible()` reads `hasGitHubAppCredentials()` (`GH_APP_ID && GH_APP_PRIVATE_KEY`; the installation ID is optional), gates on `githubAuthActiveRef` (true iff setup already activated in this process), runs setup, and returns `true` only if App auth activated. `createGitHubAuthStartGuard()` prevents concurrent in-flight setup calls. Also exports `githubInstallationsManagerRef` + `reconcileGitHubInstallations()`: the manager is set by `setupGitHubAuth()` once App auth activates, and each config-sync tick re-runs discovery against the current repo scope (no-op when the manager is null). Called from the config-sync tick so credentials arriving after the entrypoint's one-shot call (a separate process) become usable without a pod restart. |
| `runtime/spawn-env.ts` | `buildSpawnEnv(opts)` — builds the environment for a Claude spawn with an optional `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER` hint that routes multi-org GitHub calls to the right installation token. Takes `kind` (`"loop"` / `"cron"` / `"dm"`), `id` (for warn messaging), `owner` (resolved owner, if any) and `extraEnv`; returns `extraEnv` merged with the hint when an owner is known, untouched otherwise. Cron spawns (no repo context) get the default installation's owner; loop spawns get the dispatched item's repo owner; DM spawns carry no hint since Slack DMs aren't repo-scoped. Also exports `defaultOwnerOf(snapshot)` — the default owner of an `InstallationsSnapshot` (the pinned installation, else the lowest id; `null` when none). Used by `boot.ts` for the cron handler. |
| `scripts/bin/git-credential-shipwright.sh` | Git credential helper (answers `get` for `https://github.com/`; `store`/`erase` are no-ops) that reads the token written by the App auth path. When a `gh-token.d/` directory sits next to `$GH_TOKEN_FILE` (App auth) the owner comes from the `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER` environment variable — **not** from the request path git sends — and that owner's token file in `gh-token.d/` is used; an unset hint, or an owner with no token file, yields no credentials plus a stderr message, never another owner's or the default token. Without `gh-token.d/` (PAT auth) the single token file is used and the hint is ignored. |
| `scripts/bin/gh` | `gh` wrapper that exports `GH_TOKEN` from the token file before exec'ing the real `gh` (stripping its own directory from `PATH`). Under App auth it requires `SHIPWRIGHT_GH_OWNER` and uses `gh-token.d/<lowercase-owner>`; an unset hint or an owner with no token file fails with an error (no default-token fallback). In PAT mode (no token file) it passes through. |
| `runtime/gh-token-files.ts` | Atomic token-file layer (temp file + rename, mode 0600). `gh-token` always holds the default installation's token; `gh-token.d/<lowercase-owner>` holds per-owner tokens for every usable installation, even a single one (stale entries are pruned; the directory is kept). Exports `writeTokenFiles()`, `writeFileAtomic()`, `validateOwner()`. |
| `docs/github-multi-org.md` | Operator and org-admin guide for the multi-org GitHub App: how discovery and per-owner routing work, setup, the admin installations card, troubleshooting. Documents the `runtime/github-installations*.ts`, `runtime/gh-token-files.ts` and credential-helper files in this table. |
| `runtime/github-installations.ts` | GitHub App installation discovery and selection. `discoverInstallations()` lists the App's installations (App JWT, paginated); `selectInstallations()` is a pure narrowing to this agent's repo-scope owners, with `GH_APP_INSTALLATION_ID` as an optional pin and the default being the pin, else the lowest selected id. Also hosts `GitHubInstallationsManager`, which mints per-installation tokens and reconciles on scope changes. |
| `runtime/github-installations-reporter.ts` | `HttpGitHubInstallationsReporter` — fire-and-forget `PUT /agents/:id/github-installations` of the manager's installation state (owner, installation id, health, constant-string `lastError`; never tokens). Posts on state-signature change and on a 30-minute heartbeat (`INSTALLATIONS_HEARTBEAT_MS`). `NoopGitHubInstallationsReporter` is the default when unconfigured. |
| `runtime/shipwright-config-client.ts` | `ShipwrightConfigClient` (DI interface) + `RecordedShipwrightConfigClient` (cassette-backed test double). The HTTP implementation was consolidated into `HttpShipwrightRuntimeClient` (`shipwright-runtime-client.ts`), wired via `getAgentConfigBundle()` as the `configClient` adapter in `entrypoint-main.ts`. |
| `runtime/shipwright-runtime-client.ts` | Unified runtime client for the agent-facing admin API methods. Exports `ShipwrightClientError` (typed, with `statusCode`), `ShipwrightRuntimeClient` (DI interface: `getAgentConfigBundle()`, `listAgentCronJobs()`, `reconcileSystemCrons()`) and `HttpShipwrightRuntimeClient` (typed HTTP implementation via `openapi-fetch`, using `lib/admin-types.ts`). |
| `runtime/sync-config-clone.ts` | Auto-clone newly-configured repos on config sync. `syncClonedRepos(deps)` is called from the config-sync tick: it plans clones with `computeMissingClones()` from `lib/clone-plan.ts` (the shared planner; it lives in `lib/` because the runtime Dockerfile stage copies `lib/`) and clones each missing repo via `gh repo clone`, catching and logging per-repo failures so one error never blocks the rest or crashes the tick. Exports `SyncConfigCloneDeps` (DI: `getScopedRepos()`, `reposDir`, injectable `exists()` / `cloneRepo()` / `removePartialClone()`), `makeCloneRepo(spawn?)`, `buildProductionDeps(opts)` and `readRemoteOwner`. The `gh` child is spawned **asynchronously** (`Bun.spawn` + `await proc.exited`), never `Bun.spawnSync`, which would block the event loop serving the liveness/readiness probes; a module-level in-flight set guards overlapping ticks (config sync is scheduled with a bare `setInterval`). A repo missing on disk stays missing and is retried next tick. |
| `runtime/cron-handler.ts` | Cron runtime: `handleCronRequest()` runs a cron prompt through Claude and posts the result to Slack. Supports `preCheck` scripts, `silent` suppression, channel vs. DM delivery, and `onPost` / `onSession` callbacks. **Slack-optional:** `CronHandlerDeps.slack` is `WebClient \| undefined` — on a chat-only agent a completed job is still recorded via `cronRunReporter.completeRun()` but Slack delivery is skipped rather than throwing `invalid_auth`. Reporting is fire-and-forget through `CronRunReporter`: `createRun()` at start, `completeRun()` / `skipRun()` at completion, `recordProgress()` (5 s debounce, `PROGRESS_PUSH_DEBOUNCE_MS`) from the runner's `onProgress` callback so token totals survive an OOM/deploy-kill mid-run, and `recordSessionId()` from `onEarlySessionId` so a crashed or timed-out run still leaves a resumable session id. A `ClaudeTimeoutError` with `partialModelUsage` is attached as `modelBreakdown` so a timed-out run's partial consumption is recorded. `CronHandlerDeps.spawner` is an optional `typeof Bun.spawn` so tests avoid spawning real preCheck processes. Exports `formatCronMessage(jobId, prompt)` (prefixes `[Cron job: <jobId>]` and the current time) and `buildTokenPayload(usage, modelUsage, extras?)`, which forwards token counts plus run telemetry (`contextBaseline`, `turns`, `toolCalls`, `skillUsage`, `contextFingerprint`, `pluginVersion`, `claudeCodeVersion`) on every completion, skip and failure path. |
| `runtime/cron-failure-reporter.ts` | `reportCronFailure(cronId, err, deps)` — surfaces thrown dispatch errors (loop dispatch or regular `handleCronRequest`) like any other failed cron run: `createRun()` for the tick, then `completeRun()` with outcome `"failed"` and `{error: message}`, so the failure appears as an `AgentCronRun` row in the run history rather than only in pod stdout. Also calls `reportClaudeError(sentryClient, err)`, which downgrades expected-ceiling `ClaudeTimeoutError`s from `captureException` to `captureMessage` to avoid error-patrol re-triggers. Exports `reportCronFailure()` and `markCronRunFailureReported`; requires a `CronRunReporter` (callers pass the Noop fallback) and treats `sentryClient` as optional. |
| `runtime/claude-version.ts` | Claude Code CLI version detection, run once at startup: `detectClaudeCodeVersion(exec, timeoutMs = 5000)` runs `claude --version` and returns the first semver in the output, or `"unknown"` on any exec failure, non-semver output or timeout (never throws). Also exports `parseClaudeVersion()`, `bunExec` and `UNKNOWN_CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION`. `boot.ts` stores the result in `claudeVersionState` (`health.ts`), logs it, and `GET /health` reports it as `claudeCodeVersion`. The installed version is pinned by the `CLAUDE_CODE_VERSION` build ARG in `runtime/Dockerfile` (asserted against `claude --version` at build time, with `DISABLE_AUTOUPDATER=1`). |
| `runtime/cleanup-after-days-ref.ts` | Mutable box holding the agent's most recently synced `cleanupAfterDays` policy field: `createCleanupAfterDaysRef()` → `CleanupAfterDaysRef` (`get()` → `number`, default `14`; `hasSynced()`; `set(value)`) and the process-wide `cleanupAfterDaysRef` singleton, populated on every config-sync tick from `bundle.cleanupAfterDays`. `hasSynced()` lets readers fall back to the hardcoded default until a first sync lands (so a persistent sync failure is distinguishable from a synced value). `readCleanupAfterDays(workspacePath)` is the reader used by the worktree reaper. Pure, zero-I/O. |
| `runtime/cleanup-merged-worktrees-ref.ts` | Same pattern for the `cleanupMergedWorktrees` policy field: `createCleanupMergedWorktreesRef()` → `CleanupMergedWorktreesRef` (`get()` → `boolean`, default `true`; `hasSynced()`; `set(value)`), the `cleanupMergedWorktreesRef` singleton, and `readCleanupMergedWorktrees(workspacePath)`. Populated from every config-sync tick. |
| `runtime/worktree-reaper.ts` | Worktree reaper — a pure-filesystem background pass (no GitHub or task-store calls) that force-removes stale `worktrees/<repo>-<branch>` directories. `reconcileStaleWorktrees(deps)` returns immediately when `cleanupMergedWorktrees` is off; otherwise it lists `${SHIPWRIGHT_WORKTREE_DIR}/` (default `<workspace>/worktrees`), attributes each directory to a scoped repo by longest-prefix match (`resolveOwningRepo()`), filters by age (`cleanupAfterDays`, 14 days until the first sync) and runs `git worktree remove --force` for stale matches. Scoped repos arrive as `org/repo` (from `bundle.repos` via `agent-repos-ref.ts`) and are normalized to bare names via `splitOrgRepo()` to compare with directory names; when two scoped entries share a bare name (`org-a/widget` + `org-b/widget`) the worktree is ambiguous, logged distinctly, and skipped so the wrong org's clone is never cleaned. Per-directory try/catch isolates failures. `buildProductionDeps()` wires real fs/git; `boot.ts` runs it as the runtime's own periodic pass. |
| `runtime/agent-repos-ref.ts` | Mutable box holding the agent's most recently synced scoped repos (`org/repo` strings): `createAgentReposRef()` → `AgentReposRef` (`get()` → `string[]`, `set(repos)`) and the process-wide `agentReposRef` singleton, populated from every config-sync tick's `bundle.repos`. Lets consumers (the worktree reaper, extensions) read a live view of the repo scope without closing over a single `syncConfig()` snapshot. Pure, zero-I/O. |
| `runtime/cron-run-reporter.ts` | `CronRunReporter` interface (`createRun()`, `completeRun()`, `skipRun()`, `recordProgress()`, `recordSessionId()`) + `HttpCronRunReporter` (sends requests to the admin API) and `NoopCronRunReporter` (test/default). `createRun()` returns a `runId`; `completeRun()` / `skipRun()` carry token usage, cost, outcome metadata, an optional per-model breakdown (`ModelBreakdownEntry[]`: `{model, inputTokens, outputTokens, cacheReadTokens, cacheCreationTokens, costUsd}`), run telemetry (`ContextBaselineEntry`, `SkillUsageEntry`) and an optional `sessionId`, captured on every outcome (from the result, or from the `sessionId` that `ClaudeTimeoutError` / `ClaudeRunError` carry) and persisted at capture time so a process death between capture and settle still leaves a resumable session. `recordProgress()` is a fire-and-forget mid-run PATCH pushing `modelBreakdown` and `lastHeartbeatAt`. Injected into `handleCronRequest()` and extension dispatchers. |
| `runtime/run-telemetry.ts` | Pure per-run measurement accumulator fed by `claude.ts`'s stream consumer: `RunTelemetryAccumulator` with `observeContent(blocks)` (tool-call counting deduped by `tool_use` id; a `Skill` tool_use switches the current attribution bucket to `skill:<name>`, an `Agent`/`Task` tool_use records `subagent_type`) and `observeUsage(messageId, model, usage, parentToolUseId?)` (first-turn baseline capture — `contextTokens = input + cacheCreation + cacheRead`, independent of cache warmth — plus turn counting and last-wins bucket accrual; a turn carrying `parent_tool_use_id` is charged to `agent:<type>` and never becomes the baseline). `snapshot()` returns `RunTelemetry { firstTurn?, turns, toolCalls, skillUsage[] }`, surfaced as `ClaudeRunResult.telemetry` and as `partialTelemetry` on `ClaudeRunError` / `ClaudeTimeoutError` / `ClaudeAbortedError`. A resumed (`-r`) session drops `firstTurn` since it replays history. No I/O. |
| `runtime/context-stamp.ts` | Always-loaded-context fingerprint: `computeContextStamp(deps)` hashes the workspace `CLAUDE.md`, the files it `@`-imports (one hop; code spans/fences skipped like Claude Code's import parser), every `.claude/rules/**/*.md` without a `paths:` frontmatter, and the plugin version into `contextFingerprint` (sha256[:12]) plus `pluginVersion` / `claudeCodeVersion`. `createContextStampReader({workspace, pluginJsonPath, claudeCodeVersion})` is the fs-backed production reader, read once per run by the cron handler (`contextStamp` dep) so `AgentCronRun.contextFingerprint` groups runs by what the model was given. Also exports `extractImports()`, `hasPathsFrontmatter()`, `tryComputeContextStamp()`. |
| `runtime/chat-token-reporter.ts` | `ChatTokenReporter` interface (async `recordSession(usage?, totalCostUsd?, modelUsage?)`, where `modelUsage` is the Claude CLI's camelCase per-model map) + `HttpChatTokenReporter` (POSTs per-session Slack chat token usage to `POST /agents/:id/chat-tokens/daily`) and `NoopChatTokenReporter`. Injected into the Slack event handler and called at each session completion (DM, mention, reaction): with `modelUsage` it reports per model, otherwise it falls back to a single entry using the live model from `liveClaudeConfig.model`. `formatDailyDate(date, timeZone?)` formats `YYYY-MM-DD` in an IANA timezone (agent timezone when unspecified). Fire-and-forget: POST errors are swallowed as warnings. |
| `runtime/slack-thread-status-tracker.ts` | Per-thread reference counter: `ThreadStatusTracker` with `enter(key) → boolean` (true only on the 0→1 transition) and `exit(key) → boolean` (true only on 1→0). Each Slack event handler in `slack.ts` calls `enter()` / `exit()` unconditionally around its progress `start()` / `finish()` (closure-scoped per app instance, never module-level, so test instances stay isolated). The booleans select the seed card's title (`"Queued…"` vs `"Thinking…"`) and the `session_status` the stream closes with (`"processing"` vs `"active"`). `exit()` on a key already at 0 is a no-op returning `false`. |
| `runtime/slack.ts` | Slack event handler: `createSlackApp()` — Bolt Socket Mode app handling DMs, `app_mention`, `reaction_added`, file attachments, voice transcription and Slack-initiated stream cancellation (`agent_session_stopped`). `dispatchMarkers()` processes response markers (`[silent]`, `[upload:path]`, `[speak:text]`, `[react:emoji]`, `[plan:url]`) — strips them from the posted message and executes the side effects. Accepts an injected `ChatTokenReporter`. Gates: `isAllowedSlackSender()` (member restriction), `isTrialExpired()` (blocks inbound messages once the agent's trial has lapsed; the admin's lockdown sweeper is the other half) and `isAccountPaused()` (replies with `ACCOUNT_PAUSED_NOTICE`). **Progress:** each handler builds a `SlackProgress` (`slack-progress.ts`) whose `onProgress` is passed to the runner along with `extraEnv` carrying `SLACK_CHANNEL_ID` and `SLACK_THREAD_TS`; every message gets its own `chat.startStream` / `appendStream` / `stopStream` lifecycle in timeline mode. A closure-scoped `liveStreams` registry maps open streams so the `agent_session_stopped` handler can mark the matching run externally stopped (further stream calls become no-ops) and reset the thread status via `agents.sessions.setStatus`, avoiding cascading `message_not_in_streaming_state` errors. `task_update` chunks reuse one stable `id` per run and close with an explicit `complete` (or `error`) status; the final reply is delivered as its own `markdown_text` chunk, falling back to `say()` if delivery fails, so a reply is never silently dropped. Channel and group threads pass `recipient_team_id` / `recipient_user_id` to `startStream()`; DM streams omit them. |
| `runtime/slack-startup.ts` | Slack (re)start decision logic + live-client box. `startSlackIfPossible(deps)` starts the Bolt app if — and only if — credentials are complete right now AND Bolt hasn't already started; returns `true` only when this call actually started it. It exists because the Bolt app and `WebClient` were once built from a static boot-time snapshot, so late-arriving credentials (a provisioning race) left the agent offline until restart. `boot.ts` calls it from two sites sharing one `slackStartDeps` — Step 7 at boot and every config-sync tick (60 s). `createSlackStartGuard()` / `slackStartGuard` — a process-wide in-flight guard — make overlapping calls safe; tests build their own. `slackClientRef` / `createSlackClientRef()` hold the live client for cron delivery. |
| `runtime/health.ts` | Health server: `startHealthServer(port, cronDeps?, clock?, graceMs?, sentryClient?)` — the Kubernetes liveness probe. `GET /health` returns `{ ok: true, slack: "connected"\|"disconnected", claudeCodeVersion }` (200) or `{ ok: false, slack: "disconnected", ... }` (500) when the Slack socket has been continuously down longer than `graceMs` (`SLACK_DOWN_GRACE_MS`, default 90 s). `claudeCodeVersion` is detected at startup, or `"unknown"`. `POST /cron` dispatches cron prompts via `cron-handler.ts`; when `sentryClient` is injected, unhandled errors are reported via `reportClaudeError()` before the 500 (a `ValidationError` is an expected outcome and is not captured). Exports `slackState`, `markSlackConnected()`, `markSlackDisconnected(clock)`, `claudeVersionState`, `createHealthApp`, `DEFAULT_HEALTH_PORT`. |
| `runtime/log-prefix.ts` | `buildLogPrefix(agentId, timestamp)` — console log prefix: `[timestamp] [agent:agentId]` when `agentId` is set and non-empty, `[timestamp]` otherwise. Used by the console monkeypatch in `boot.ts` to tag logs with the agent ID in aggregated multi-agent log views. |

## Shared library (`lib/`)

See [shared-lib.md](./shared-lib.md) for the full module list; the files below are the ones the tables above lean on.

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `lib/pricing.ts` | Per-model token rates and context windows shared by the runtime and admin: `RATES` (per-million-token input/output rates per model key, including the 5.x ids), `CONTEXT_WINDOW` (input-token window per rate key), `calculateCost(usage, model)` and `normalizeModelToRateKey(model)` (5.x ids map to themselves; bare `sonnet` / `opus` / `haiku` aliases map to their 5.5 keys). |
| `lib/cli-flags.ts` | Shared argv parser `parseFlags(argv, flagSpecs, kinds?)`. Pure, no env fallback; unknown flags are ignored. Plain `--flag value` / `--flag=value` string flags (`undefined` when absent), plus optional `kinds.booleans` (presence flags, `false` when absent) and `kinds.multi` (repeatable flags collected in order, `[]` when absent). |

## Database

| File | Purpose |
|---|---|
| `admin/src/prisma-client.ts` | Single factory `createAdminPrismaClient(databaseUrl, opts = {})` that builds an adapter-backed `PrismaClient` for Prisma 7 (which removed the bundled query engine): admin talks to Postgres via the `PrismaPg` adapter wrapping a `pg.Pool` (`createAdminPgPool`). Centralizing the setup gives `admin-boot.ts`, dev/CI scripts and integration suites consistent pool tuning (`connectionTimeoutMillis: DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`, default 10 s, tolerant of cold Cloud SQL connections) and uniform `disposeExternalPool: true` semantics (so every `prisma.$disconnect()` releases the pool). Exports `DB_CONNECT_TIMEOUT_MS`, `resolveAdminPoolObservabilityConfig()`, `observeAdminPool()` and the factory; when `opts.onPoolObserved` is set the pool is instrumented for hold tracking (the callback receives the pool and a stop function for shutdown). See [observability.md](./observability.md). |
| `admin/prisma/schema/` | The Prisma multi-file schema (`DATABASE_URL_SHIPWRIGHT_ADMIN`): `schema.prisma` holds the platform models and `coding.prisma` the coding-extension models; migrations are in `admin/prisma/migrations/`. **Prisma 7:** the `prisma-client` generator (ESM, driver-adapter based) replaces `prisma-client-js`, the datasource block no longer accepts a `url` field — the connection string for CLI/Migrate lives in `admin/prisma.config.ts` — and the runtime client connects through the `PrismaPg` adapter created in `admin/src/prisma-client.ts`. |
